questions.q: What is the role of the classifier function in Resource Governor?
options: A scalar UDF, run once per new session, that inspects things like APP_NAME() or SUSER_NAME() and returns which workload group that session belongs in
A stored procedure that automatically rewrites slow queries
A function that caps how much CPU the entire instance can use
A DMV that reports historical CPU usage per database
questions.explain: The classifier function runs per session on connection and returns the name of the workload group to route that session into.

questions.q: How do workload groups and resource pools relate to each other?
options: Each workload group is bound to exactly one resource pool, which defines the actual CPU/memory limits and floors enforced for sessions in that group
A single resource pool can only ever serve one individual session at a time
Workload groups and resource pools are two names for the exact same object
Resource pools are bound to workload groups in a many-to-many relationship with no limit
questions.explain: Sessions are classified into a workload group, and each workload group uses exactly one resource pool for its actual resource limits.

questions.q: What do MAX_CPU_PERCENT and MAX_MEMORY_PERCENT do on a resource pool?
options: Cap what that pool can consume even under contention with other pools
Guarantee that pool a fixed percentage of resources at all times, whether or not it's in use
Automatically tune the underlying queries in that pool to use less CPU
Disable the pool entirely once the percentage is reached
questions.explain: MAX_CPU_PERCENT and MAX_MEMORY_PERCENT are upper bounds on what a pool can consume, even when the instance is under contention.

questions.q: In the reporting-vs-OLTP scenario this lesson describes, what does MIN_CPU_PERCENT on the OLTP pool guarantee?
options: A CPU floor the OLTP workload can always fall back on when the instance is under CPU pressure and multiple pools are competing
That the OLTP pool can never use more than the minimum percentage specified
That the reporting pool will automatically be disabled whenever OLTP traffic increases
That OLTP queries will always run faster than reporting queries regardless of their own design
questions.explain: MIN_CPU_PERCENT reserves a guaranteed floor for a pool specifically for situations where pools are competing for CPU.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what does capping a reporting workload's resource pool NOT fix?
options: It doesn't make the reporting queries themselves faster — index tuning and query rewrites are still needed for that; it only isolates the workload's resource footprint
It doesn't stop the reporting workload from ever running on the instance
It doesn't apply to Power BI or SSRS connections specifically
It doesn't require ALTER RESOURCE GOVERNOR RECONFIGURE to take effect
questions.explain: Resource Governor isolates how much of the instance's resources a workload can consume; it does nothing to make that workload's own queries run faster.
